log.title: Delivery log
log.note: One row per notification sent to a channel. A failed row says on whose side it failed; open it to see every attempt and what the receiving service answered.

sideExplain.yagra: Yagra stopped before sending: the target address was refused, or the request could not be built. Check the channel settings in Yagra.
sideExplain.network: Sent, but nothing answered: a timeout, a refused connection, DNS or TLS. Check the path from Yagra to the service (firewall, proxy, DNS).
sideExplain.remote: The receiving service answered and refused. The status and its answer say why — usually a wrong key or URL, or a limit on the service side.
sideExplain.unknown: Written by a newer version of Yagra.

thresholds.note: Hierarchical overrides: profile → group → node. The most specific scope wins.
thresholds.explainer: Every alert Yagra raises from polling comes from a rule here, node up/down included. Each is evaluated live on every matching poll sample; the most-specific scope wins, and a rule at “every node” is the fleet default. Warning/critical bounds and the number of consecutive breaches before it commits (anti-flap) are per rule. Two exceptions worth knowing: reachability has no bounds, because a node either answered or it did not — only the breach count applies; and the four interface metrics Yagra computes rather than collects (if_in_util_pct / if_out_util_pct / if_in_bps / if_out_bps) are evaluated once a minute rather than per poll, so their breach count counts minutes — or polls, on a node polled less often than once a minute.
thresholds.noLiveness: No reachability rule exists, so a node going down raises no alert and sends no notification. Node state on the Nodes page still updates. Add a rule on Reachability to start paging again.
thresholds.unavailable: Threshold management is unavailable in skeleton mode.
thresholds.emptySub: Add a metric threshold scoped to a profile, group, or node.

addModal.title: Add threshold rule

scopeIdNoun.global: This rule applies to every node. Anything you set at a profile, group or node scope overrides it.

addModal.scopeIdHintMany: Every {{noun}} this rule targets. Pick as many as apply — one rule, not one each.
addModal.dwellTitle: Consecutive breaches: readings that must cross the bound in a row before the alert fires
addModal.boundsHint: Fill either row, or both. Filling both alerts outside a band — a value that drops too low OR climbs too high, from one rule. Every bound is optional. Breaches is how many consecutive readings must cross a bound before the alert fires; higher values suppress flapping (rapid on/off alerts).
addModal.folderGroupHint: Applies to this group and every group inside it. A rule on a group further in wins over this one.
addModal.legacyTagHint: Legacy scope: matches a tag on the node, or one it inherits from its folder — not the folder tree itself. Kept so existing rules keep working; new rules use a folder group.
addModal.interfaceHint: This rule covers one port of one node. Port rules are created from a node’s Interfaces tab, where the port is already in view; here you can change its bounds or delete it.
addModal.rowMatchHint: For a metric reported once per memory pool, CPU or sensor: apply this rule only to rows with this name. * matches anything, and case is ignored. Leave it empty for every row. At the same scope, a rule with a row name wins over one without for the rows it names — so it can loosen or tighten one pool beside the rule for all of them.
